ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating Time Series Data Quality with Pre-trained LLMs
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the performance of pre-trained LLMs (such as T5 and BART) on a variety of real-world time series datasets from diverse domains (e.g., electricity load forecasting, exchange rate forecasting, traffic forecasting, weather forecasting). Train these LLMs to predict human-labeled quality scores for time series samples, using a range of input formats (e.g., tabular, graphical, textual descriptions). Consider using cross-validation and multiple metrics (e.g., correlation, mean squared error) to evaluate the quality of LLM predictions. 
CONTROLS: Compare LLM performance to a naive baseline (e.g., predicting constant quality scores), as well as to a simple autoregressive model (e.g., ARIMA) that leverages traditional time series analysis techniques. 
COST: 120000
PREDICTION: I expect the LLMs to outperform the naive baseline and the ARIMA model, particularly on datasets from domains where the LLMs have been pre-trained (e.g., weather forecasting). However, the performance might degrade on datasets from less-represented domains (e.g., handwriting recognition, spacecraft telemetry anomaly detection).

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Investigating Time Series Representation Effectiveness for LLMs
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of different time series representation techniques (e.g., lagged variables, Fourier features, wavelet coefficients, statistical moments) on LLM performance in predicting time series quality scores. Experiment with varying representation dimensions, pooling methods, and combinations of these techniques. For example, compare the effectiveness of representing time series as lagged variables, Fourier features, or wavelet coefficients when fed into the LLM.
CONTROLS: As in proposal 1 (Investigating Time Series Data Quality with Pre-trained LLMs), include a naive baseline and an ARIMA model for comparison.
COST: 150000
PREDICTION: I expect the optimal representation technique to interact with the LLM architecture, and that a combination of techniques (e.g., lagged variables and Fourier features) might yield better performance than any single technique. The effectiveness of different representations might also depend on the time series domain and quality characteristics.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Temporally-Informed Prompt Engineering for Time Series Quality Assessment
PROPOSAL: Develop and evaluate temporally-informed prompts that guide LLMs to focus on quality-relevant time series characteristics, such as trends, seasonality, and anomalies. Design prompts that adapt to different time series domains and quality criteria. For example, for a weather forecasting dataset, a prompt might focus on the presence and magnitude of seasonal trends, while for an exchange rate forecasting dataset, it might focus on the presence of anomalies or trends.
CONTROLS: As in proposals 1 and 2, include a naive baseline and an ARIMA model for comparison. Additionally, compare different prompt engineering techniques, such as manual prompt design, neural prompt learning, and template-based prompting.
COST: 180000
PREDICTION: I expect temporally-informed prompts to improve LLM performance in predicting time series quality scores, particularly on domains where the prompts are tailored to specific characteristics (e.g., weather forecasting). However, the effectiveness of different prompts might depend on the LLM architecture and the representation technique used.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating Time Series Data Quality with Fine-Tuned LLMs
PROPOSAL: Revisit proposal 1 by fine-tuning pre-trained LLMs on time series datasets from diverse domains, rather than relying on the general-purpose quality prediction task. Expect that fine-tuning will enable the LLMs to learn domain-specific quality characteristics and improve performance. Also, investigate the impact of fine-tuning dataset size, training epochs, and learning rates on LLM performance.
CONTROLS: Compare the fine-tuned LLMs to the previous LLMs (as in proposal 1) and the ARIMA model. Evaluate the impact of fine-tuning on the representation effectiveness and temporally-informed prompt engineering.
COST: 190000
PREDICTION: I expect fine-tuning to significantly improve LLM performance in predicting time series quality scores, particularly on domains where the fine-tuning data is abundant. However, the incremental benefit of fine-tuning might diminish on domains with limited fine-tuning data.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Investigating Simulated Annealing for LLM-based Time Series Quality Optimization
PROPOSAL: Apply simulated annealing to optimize the quality prediction scores of LLMs for time series data, by iteratively perturbing the input representation, prompt, or fine-tuning objectives. Evaluate the impact of simulated annealing on improving LLM performance, convergence speed, and computational efficiency.
CONTROLS: As in previous proposals, include a naive baseline, the ARIMA model, and comparison with the fine-tuned LLMs. Investigate the effect of simulated annealing on representation effectiveness and temporally-informed prompt engineering.
COST: 200000
PREDICTION: I expect simulated annealing to improve LLM performance in predicting time series quality scores, particularly on datasets with noisy or missing values, by allowing the LLMs to explore a more diverse solution space. However, the optimal cooling schedule and perturbation rates might need to be carefully tuned for each dataset and LLM architecture.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Evaluating Transferability of LLM-based Time Series Quality Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate the transferability of LLM-based time series quality models across different datasets and domains. Fine-tune LLMs on a subset of datasets and evaluate their performance on unseen datasets. Compare the transferability of LLMs with different architectures, representation techniques, and fine-tuning objectives. Also, investigate the impact of transferability on the quality prediction scores.
CONTROLS: Use a subset of datasets from the experimental domains (electricity load forecasting, exchange rate forecasting, traffic forecasting, weather forecasting, handwriting recognition, spacecraft telemetry anomaly detection) for fine-tuning and evaluation. Compare the transferability of fine-tuned LLMs with the ARIMA model.
COST: 220000
PREDICTION: I expect the transferability of fine-tuned LLMs to be domain-dependent, with better transferability on datasets from related domains (e.g., weather forecasting and traffic forecasting). However, transferability might degrade on datasets from less-related domains (e.g., handwriting recognition).

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Multimodal Temporally-Informed Prompt Engineering for Time Series Quality Assessment
PROPOSAL: Enhance temporally-informed prompt engineering by incorporating multiple modalities (e.g., text, images, graphs) and prompt-augmentation techniques (e.g., data augmentation, adversarial perturbations). Evaluate the impact of multimodal prompt engineering on LLM performance, convergence speed, and computational efficiency. Investigate the effect of multimodal prompt engineering on representation effectiveness and transferability.
CONTROLS: As in previous proposals, include a naive baseline, the ARIMA model, and comparison with the fine-tuned LLMs. Also, investigate the transferability of multimodal fine-tuned LLMs across different datasets and domains.
COST: 250000
PREDICTION: I expect multimodal temporally-informed prompt engineering to improve LLM performance in predicting time series quality scores, particularly on datasets with multiple data modalities (e.g., sensor readings and images). However, the optimal combination of modalities and prompt-augmentation techniques might need to be carefully tuned for each dataset and LLM architecture.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Investigating Domain-Specific Quality Metrics for Time Series Data
PROPOSAL: Develop domain-specific quality metrics for time series data, tailored to the characteristics of each experimental domain (electricity load forecasting, exchange rate forecasting, traffic forecasting, weather forecasting, handwriting recognition, spacecraft telemetry anomaly detection). Evaluate the effectiveness of these metrics in predicting LLM performance and time series quality. Investigate the interaction between domain-specific metrics and LLM architectures.
CONTROLS: Compare the domain-specific metrics to traditional quality metrics (e.g., rmse, mae) and LLM performance on each experimental domain. Also, investigate the transferability of domain-specific metrics across different datasets and domains.
COST: 280000
PREDICTION: I expect domain-specific quality metrics to improve LLM performance in predicting time series quality scores, particularly on datasets from specific domains. However, the development of effective domain-specific metrics might require extensive knowledge of each domain's characteristics and nuances.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Hierarchical Time Series Representation Effectiveness for LLMs
PROPOSAL: Enhance time series representation effectiveness by leveraging hierarchical structures (e.g., seasonal, trend, residual components) in time series data. Investigate the impact of hierarchical representation on LLM performance, convergence speed, and computational efficiency. Compare the effectiveness of hierarchical representation with traditional representation techniques.
CONTROLS: As in previous proposals, include a naive baseline, the ARIMA model, and comparison with the fine-tuned LLMs. Also, investigate the interaction between hierarchical representation and multimodal temporally-informed prompt engineering.
COST: 300000
PREDICTION: I expect hierarchical time series representation to improve LLM performance in predicting time series quality scores, particularly on datasets with clear seasonal or trend components. However, the optimal hierarchical structure and representation technique might need to be carefully tuned for each dataset and LLM architecture.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Generalizable LLM-based Time Series Quality Assessment Framework
PROPOSAL: Develop a framework that integrates the findings from previous experiments and proposes a generalizable approach for LLM-based time series quality assessment. Investigate the combination of fine-tuned LLMs, hierarchical time series representation, multimodal temporally-informed prompt engineering, simulated annealing, and domain-specific quality metrics to achieve robust and transferable time series quality assessment.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the proposed framework with individual components and traditional methods (e.g., ARIMA, influence functions). Investigate the transferability of the framework across different datasets and domains.
COST: 320000
PREDICTION: I expect the proposed framework to outperform individual components and traditional methods, providing a significant improvement in time series quality assessment accuracy and robustness. However, the optimal combination of components might need to be fine-tuned for each dataset and domain, and the framework might require careful tuning for each specific use case.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leveraging Synthetic Text Datasets for Inference-based Anonymization Research
PROPOSAL: Utilize the Realistic Synthetic Text Dataset (RSTD), a recently proposed benchmark for text anonymization, to create a set of systematically varied synthetic texts that simulate different real-world scenarios. These scenarios will include varying degrees of personal attribute mention (e.g., names, locations), contextual cues, and explicit statements about sensitive information. We will train multiple small language models (e.g., BART, T5) on these datasets to evaluate their anonymization capabilities against an adversarial LLM (e.g., GPT-4) that attempts to infer personal attributes from the anonymized text.
CONTROLS: Comparison to a baseline set of strong industry-grade anonymizers (e.g., Google's efforts for Healthcare), as well as ablation experiments to understand the impact of the synthetic dataset characteristics and LLM architectures on inference attack success.
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Results suggest that even smaller LLMs under modest compute budgets can achieve a reasonable trade-off between privacy and readability, particularly when confronted with synthetic texts engineering contextual features to conceal personal information. However, attacks may still succeed in particularly well-informed settings or for highly skilled adversaries.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Refining for Inference Defense in Small Language Models
PROPOSAL: Develop an adaptive refining mechanism that tunes small LLMs (e.g., RoBERTa variants) based on the strength of the adversarial feedback from the LLM adversary. This mechanism will iteratively refine the anonymized text while considering the adversary's attempts to infer personal attributes. The LLMs will analyze the effectiveness of their defense by estimating the adversary's confidence, thereby adjusting their refining process to achieve an optimal trade-off between privacy and readability.
CONTROLS: Comparison to the baseline LLM from proposal 1 (with and without adaptive refining) and ablation experiments to determine the relative importance of refining strategies such as temperature scaling and formatted-expression validation.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Results demonstrate improved LLM resilience to inference attacks through adaptive refining, yielding better protection of sensitive information without compromising text coherence or readability.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Leveraging Synthetic Text Datasets for Inference-based Anonymization Research with Adversarial Pre-training
PROPOSAL: Refine proposal 1 by including an additional stage where the small LLMs receive adversarial pre-training. This pre-training will utilize a variant of the LLM adversary to provide augmented feedback that simulates the type of attacks the anonymized texts will face. This enriched pre-training phase aims to equip the small LLMs with improved defense strategies against inference-based attacks from the start. We will then evaluate the effectiveness of these pre-trained models in anonymization tasks.
CONTROLS: Retain comparison to industry-grade anonymizers and ablation studies, also adding new controls to measure the impact of adversarial pre-training on LLM performance.
COST: 800 GPU-hours (incremental to original estimate due to the added pre-training stage)
PREDICTION: The inclusion of adversarial pre-training is expected to further augment the anonymization capabilities of the small LLMs, achieving more comprehensive protection of personal attributes and sensitive information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Anonymization Sub-model Augmentation for Enhanced Privacy
PROPOSAL: Integrate a separate anonymization-focused sub-model into the existing small LLM architecture. This sub-model will be trained exclusively to identify and distort contextual cues that contribute to inference-based attacks, allowing the main LLM to maintain text coherence while amplifying the anonymization efforts. We will then evaluate the impact of this sub-model on the overall trade-off between privacy and readability.
CONTROLS: Comparative analysis to baseline LLMs with and without the sub-model, as well as ablation experiments to understand the respective contributions of the main LLM and the anonymization sub-model.
COST: 1600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Successful integration of the anonymization sub-model is anticipated to provide a more robust defense against inference attacks, ultimately improving the anonymization process's effectiveness without compromising text readability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporalagus: De-Anonymization Pattern Detection and Obfuscation
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel approach called Temporalagus, designed to not only prevent inference attacks but also detect potential de-anonymization patterns. Small LLMs equipped with Temporalagus will attempt to anticipate and obfuscate the context-specific information sought by adversaries. This approach involves training a secondary model to infer the adversary's intent, allowing the primary LLM to adjust its anonymization strategy accordingly.
CONTROLS: Comparative analysis to baseline LLMs, as well as ablation experiments to determine the impact of different training objectives for the primary and secondary models.
COST: 2400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Results indicate that the integration of Temporalagus with small LLMs leads to a significant reduction in successful inference attacks, minimizing the risk of information disclosure.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Leveraging Synthetic Text Datasets for Inference-based Anonymization Research with Adversarial Pre-training and Task-Switching
PROPOSAL: Enhance proposal 1 by incorporating task-switching into the small LLMs' training process for adversarial pre-training. This adaptation allows the LLMs to not only anticipate the type of adversarial attacks they will face but also adjust their anonymization strategies in real-time according to the context. The LLMs will be trained to switch between anonymization and generation tasks, mimicking how they would respond in a real-world scenario.
CONTROLS: Retain comparison to industry-grade anonymizers and measure the impact of task-switching on the effectiveness of LLMs in preventing inference attacks.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours (incremental to original estimate due to the added task-switching stage)
PREDICTION: Results are expected to show a significant improvement in the LLMs' ability to defend against inference attacks and adapt to real-world scenarios, cementing their role as effective anonymization tools under modest compute budgets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Post-processing Filter: Anonymity Quality Assurer
PROPOSAL: Develop a post-processing filter designed to inspect the output of the small LLMs and detect potential vulnerabilities to inference attacks. This filter will be trained to identify areas where further anonymization is necessary, ensuring the final output is robust against inference. It will serve as a last layer of quality control before releasing the anonymized text.
CONTROLS: Comparative analysis to baseline LLMs, as well as ablation experiments to determine the impact of different filter training objectives and detection strategies.
COST: 3600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Results indicate that incorporating the post-processing filter significantly enhances the anonymization capabilities of small LLMs, ensuring a more comprehensive defense against inference attacks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Transfer Learning for Cross-Domain Anonymization
PROPOSAL: Investigate the feasibility of transferring knowledge from one domain to another when anonymizing texts. This will involve training a small LLM on a set of anonymized texts from one domain and then applying it to texts from a different domain. We will assess whether the knowledge transfer is sufficient to provide effective anonymization.
CONTROLS: Comparative analysis to baseline LLMs trained and fine-tuned on each domain individually, as well as ablation experiments to understand the contribution of different adaptation strategies.
COST: 4800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Results suggest that transfer learning allows small LLMs to adapt to new domains with a good anonymization performance, potentially reducing costs associated with re-training and increasing scalability for real-world applications.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Privacy-Utility Trade-off using Automated Metrics
PROPOSAL: Develop an automated evaluation framework to assess the privacy-utility trade-off of the anonymization methods proposed in the current set. This framework will utilize metrics such as anonymization efficiency, text coherence, and readability, along with privacy measures like inference attack success rates. We will analyze how each method affects this trade-off and inform future improvements.
CONTROLS: Comparative analysis to baseline methods, as well as ablation experiments to evaluate the sensitivity of the automated metrics.
COST: 6000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Results will provide a comprehensive understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of the proposed anonymization methods, facilitating the development of more effective strategies that achieve a better balance between privacy and utility.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Anonymization Efficacy for Real-World Scenarios: Multivariate Analysis and Error Prediction
PROPOSAL: Conduct a multivariate analysis of the anonymization methods proposed in the current set, integrating contextual and environmental factors to evaluate their efficacy in real-world scenarios. Additionally, we will develop a predictive model for estimating error rates under various conditions, enabling informed decision-making on anonymization strategies.
CONTROLS: Comparative analysis to baseline methods, as well as ablation experiments to evaluate the impact of different contextual factors and the predictive model's performance.
COST: 7200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Results will provide valuable insights into the suitability of each anonymization method for real-world applications, along with a tool for predicting error rates, thus further enhancing the development of effective anonymization strategies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Establishing the Asymptotic Behavior of Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the asymptotic convergence of Shapley values estimation methods, including KernelSHAP, unbiased KernelSHAP, and LeverageSHAP, using the framework of likely-to-be-sampled subsets and their respective weights. Utilize techniques from probability theory, such as law of large numbers, central limit theorem, and large deviations theory, to derive a set of theoretical bounds and convergences that can be empirically verified. Assume the inputs are a kernel-weighted graph structure and model outputs for subsets of features.
CONTROLS: 
- Vanilla KernelSHAP: served as a baseline for comparison.
- Unbiased KernelSHAP: included to assess the impact of bias correction on asymptotic performance.
- LeverageSHAP: tested alongside other methods to verify its improvement.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The developed theoretical framework will reveal that LeverageSHAP converges at a faster rate than KernelSHAP and unbiased KernelSHAP, while unbiased KernelSHAP may exhibit slower convergence due to bias correction, with potential failure when intermediate conditioning on partial feature sets introduces significant variance into the estimator.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Shapley Value Estimation for High-Dimensional Data with Provable Guarantees
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel Shapley value estimation algorithm for high-dimensional data that incorporates sparse approximation techniques and enjoys provable theoretical guarantees. Utilize a sparse partition of the feature space to efficiently compute marginal contributions of individual features. Develop a set of theoretical bounds and sample complexity analysis to demonstrate the scalability of the method. Consider applying SimSHAP as a subroutine to leverage pre-computed information stored in the sparse partition.
CONTROLS: 
- SimSHAP: included as the basis for pretraining the sparse partition model.
- KernelSHAP: used as a baseline for comparison to the novel method's performance.
- LeverageSHAP: evaluated for its ability to complement the proposed algorithm.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The new method will exhibit efficient scalability to high-dimensional features while providing accurate Shapley value estimates, outperforming kernel-based estimators like KernelSHAP and showing potential as a more accurate and efficient adjunct to LeverageSHAP.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparative Study of Sampling Distributions for Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Design a comprehensive experiment to compare the performance of Shapley value estimation methods with different sampling distributions, including the original unweighted sampling used in KernelSHAP and weighted sampling used in unbiased KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP. Evaluate the estimators on a variety of datasets and models, assessing their accuracy, stability, and computational efficiency. Consider using both synthetic and real-world benchmarks.
CONTROLS: 
- Vanilla KernelSHAP with unweighted sampling.
- Unbiased KernelSHAP with weighted sampling for subsets.
- LeverageSHAP with weighted sampling based on statistical leverage scores.
- The novel high-dimensional method from Proposal 2.
COST: 3000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The study will reveal that LeverageSHAP with weighted sampling based on statistical leverage scores outperforms the other methods, with potential failure in cases where the sampling distribution does not capture the underlying distribution of feature importance, highlighting the need for careful tuning of the sampling distribution.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Comparative Study of Sampling Distributions for Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Refine the experimental design for the comparative study to account for the specific characteristics of each dataset and model, such as feature correlation, dimensionality, and model complexity. Adopt a meta-learning approach to leverage information from a suite of datasets and models to identify general trends and insights about the performance of different sampling distributions. Introduce a novel adaptive sampling strategy that dynamically adjusts the sampling distribution based on the features' importance and the model's behavior.
CONTROLS: 
- Vanilla KernelSHAP with unweighted sampling.
- Unbiased KernelSHAP with weighted sampling for subsets.
- LeverageSHAP with weighted sampling based on statistical leverage scores.
- The novel high-dimensional method from Proposal 2.
- The adaptive sampling strategy as a new variant.
COST: 5000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The refined study will demonstrate that the adaptive sampling strategy offers improved accuracy and stability across a wide range of datasets and models, with potential failure when the adaptive mechanism over-compensates for the bias in the initial sampling distribution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Impact of Feature Interactions on Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Investigate how feature interactions, such as correlation and co-linearity, affect the accuracy of Shapley value estimation methods, including KernelSHAP, unbiased KernelSHAP, and LeverageSHAP. Design a set of experiments to create controlled scenarios with progressively increasing feature interactions and assess how the estimators perform under these conditions. Explore the use of data preprocessing techniques, such as feature selection or dimensionality reduction, to mitigate the effects of feature interactions.
CONTROLS: 
- Original implementations of KernelSHAP, unbiased KernelSHAP, and LeverageSHAP.
- Variants of the estimators with feature selection or dimensionality reduction applied.
COST: 4500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The study will reveal that feature interactions can significantly degrade the accuracy of Shapley value estimates, with KernelSHAP being particularly vulnerable to co-linear features, and leverage score-based sampling offering some resistance to high correlations, while the preprocessing techniques can provide some mitigation, but may fail to capture complex interactions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Time-Domain Analysis of Shapley Value Estimation: Sequential and Streaming Scenarios
PROPOSAL: Investigate the performance of Shapley value estimation methods in time-critical and streaming scenarios, where data arrives in a sequential manner. Design experiments to test how the estimators handle data streams with varying rates, characteristics, and importance, and assess their ability to provide accurate and timely explanations under these conditions. Explore the use of time-series processing techniques and incremental updating methods to improve the estimators' responsiveness and efficiency.
CONTROLS: 
- Original implementations of KernelSHAP, unbiased KernelSHAP, and LeverageSHAP.
- Incremental updating variants of the estimators.
- State-of-the-art time-series processing and streaming algorithms as baselines.
COST: 6000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The study will reveal that LeverageSHAP and incremental updating techniques can provide excellent performance in streaming scenarios, with potential failure when the stream's characteristics change too rapidly or have high variability, highlighting the importance of adapting estimators to the time-domain context.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Shapley Value Estimation for High-Dimensional Data with Provable Guarantees
PROPOSAL: Refine the sparse partition strategy used in the novel high-dimensional method to incorporate topological information about the feature space. Utilize techniques from topological data analysis to create a more informed and structured sparse partition, which should improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the Shapley value estimation. Incorporate this refinement into the larger framework and re-evaluate the method's performance in the context of the other proposals.
CONTROLS: 
- The refined novel high-dimensional method.
- Original implementations of KernelSHAP, unbiased KernelSHAP, and LeverageSHAP.
- Incremental updating variants of the estimators.
COST: 9000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The refined method will exhibit improved performance in high-dimensional feature spaces, with the incorporation of topological information providing a more sophisticated sparse partition that reduces estimation errors and computational costs, while minimizing potential failure when the underlying structure of the feature space cannot be accurately captured.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Time-Domain Analysis of Shapley Value Estimation: Sequential and Streaming Scenarios
PROPOSAL: Introduce a new adaptive streaming algorithm that leverages online learning techniques to adapt the Shapley value estimation to the evolving characteristics of the data stream in real-time. The algorithm will monitor the data stream's dynamics and adjust the estimation model accordingly, using techniques from reinforcement learning to optimize the adaptation process. Evaluate the performance of this adaptive algorithm against other methods, including the refined novel high-dimensional method, and assess its ability to provide accurate explanations in time-critical and dynamic scenarios.
CONTROLS: 
- Original implementations of KernelSHAP, unbiased KernelSHAP, and LeverageSHAP.
- Incremental updating variants of the estimators.
- The refined novel high-dimensional method.
- A baseline adaptive algorithm using traditional reinforcement learning.
COST: 12000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The adaptive streaming algorithm will demonstrate its ability to adapt quickly to changing data stream characteristics, providing accurate Shapley value estimates in real-time, but may fail to generalize well when faced with drastically new data distribution, highlighting the importance of fine-tuning the algorithm for specific use cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Large-Scale Evaluation of Shapley Value Estimation Methods on Real-World Datasets
PROPOSAL: Conduct a comprehensive evaluation of the Shapley value estimation methods proposed in this research, including the refined novel high-dimensional method and the adaptive streaming algorithm, on a suite of large-scale real-world datasets from various domains. Assess their performance in terms of accuracy, scalability, and interpretability, and identify any potential limitations or failure modes. Use this evaluation to inform the development of best practices and guidelines for the deployment of Shapley value estimation methods in real-world applications.
CONTROLS: 
- All previous methods and algorithms.
- A selection of large-scale real-world datasets from various domains.
COST: 18000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The large-scale evaluation will reveal that the refined novel high-dimensional method and the adaptive streaming algorithm can provide accurate Shapley value estimates on real-world datasets, but may fail to scale to extremely large datasets or complex models, necessitating further optimization and preprocessing techniques.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Establishing the Asymptotic Behavior of Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Refine the theoretical framework for the asymptotic behavior of Shapley value estimation, incorporating insights from the large-scale evaluation of real-world datasets. Derive new bounds and convergence results that account for the complexities and nuances of real-world data, and develop a more comprehensive understanding of the trade-offs between accuracy, scalability, and interpretability in Shapley value estimation. Use this refined framework to inform the development of future Shapley value estimation methods and algorithms.
CONTROLS: 
- All previous methods and algorithms.
- The results from the large-scale evaluation.
COST: 25000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The refined theoretical framework will provide a deeper understanding of the asymptotic behavior of Shapley value estimation, revealing that the methods and algorithms developed in this research can provide accurate and interpretable results on large-scale real-world datasets, but may still fail to capture certain nuances and complexities, highlighting the need for continued research and development in this area.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bridging the Gap Between Uniform Mass and Non-Uniform Terminal Distributions
PROPOSAL: Design an experiment to learn branched dynamics between an initial and a terminal distribution with multiple modes, allowing for non-uniform mass assignment to each terminal mode, using the Cartographer network architecture for trajectory inference and a weighted KL divergence loss to enforce the desired mass distribution.
CONTROLS: Train Cartographer on a uniform mass setting as a baseline, ablate the weighted KL divergence loss to see if the model can still learn branched dynamics, and evaluate on a synthetic dataset with ground truth branched trajectories.
COST: 4320
PREDICTION: The model will learn accurate branched dynamics and mass redistribution patterns, but may struggle with accurately assigning non-uniform mass to each terminal mode, especially when the terminal modes have different numbers of samples.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Branching Dynamics on Real-World Single-Cell RNA-Seq Data
PROPOSAL: Adapt the previous model to real-world single-cell RNA-seq data by incorporating permutation-invariant attention to focus on gene expression features relevant to cell differentiation, and train the model on two publicly available datasets (e.g., the Tabata et al. 2019 and the 10X Genomics Visium datasets) with class-balanced and class-imbalanced labels representing different cell types.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the adapted model on both class-balanced and class-imbalanced scenarios, ablate the permutation-invariant attention to see its impact on performance, and use as a baseline a standard classifier trained on the same features.
COST: 8640
PREDICTION: The model will outperform the baseline classifier on both scenarios, but its performance may degrade with class imbalance due to the challenges of capturing branched dynamics in sparse data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Quantifying the Emergence of Branching Dynamics in Perturbation Response Modeling
PROPOSAL: Extend the model to incorporate an additional perturbation response component that predicts the expected timing and location of branching events in response to gene knockouts or drug treatment, using the previously adapted model as a base and training on LiDAR-scanned terrain surfaces for a navigation domain experiment, as well as on a synthetic dataset with ground-truth perturbation timing and branching dynamics.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the perturbation response component on both the LiDAR-scanned terrain surfaces and synthetic datasets, ablate the branching dynamics component to see its impact on perturbation response modeling, and use as a baseline a standard model for predicting cell fate following perturbation.
COST: 12960
PREDICTION: The model will successfully identify and predict branching events in response to perturbation, and its performance will be positively correlated with the accuracy of the underlying branched dynamics component.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Modeling Branched Trajectories with Transition State Analysis
PROPOSAL: Incorporate transition state analysis (TSA) into the model to identify key transition states and intermediate modes in the branched trajectories, using TSA to extract informative features that capture the underlying energetic landscape and coupling between modes, and evaluating the TSA-enhanced model on a set of challenging synthetic and real-world datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare the TSA-enhanced model with the original branched dynamics model, ablate the TSA component to assess its contribution to performance, and evaluate the TSA-extracted transition states for their accuracy and relevance to the system's dynamics.
COST: 19440
PREDICTION: The TSA-enhanced model will demonstrate improved performance in recovering branched trajectories and accurately identifying key transition states, particularly in systems with complex intermediate modes and energetic landscapes.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Enhancing Evaluating Branching Dynamics on Real-World Single-Cell RNA-Seq Data with TSA and Active Learning
PROPOSAL: Integrate transition state analysis (TSA) into the previous evaluation of branched dynamics on real-world single-cell RNA-seq data, using TSA to guide active learning by identifying the most informative samples for labeling, and evaluating the TSA-guided active learning approach on a set of challenging real-world datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare the TSA-guided active learning approach with the standard evaluation approach, ablate the TSA component to assess its contribution to active learning performance, and evaluate the quality of the samples selected by TSA.
COST: 25920
PREDICTION: The TSA-guided active learning approach will demonstrate improved performance in evaluating branched dynamics on real-world single-cell RNA-seq data, particularly in systems with limited labeled samples, by effectively identifying the most informative samples for labeling.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Bounds for Branched Dynamics with Non-Uniform Terminal Distributions
PROPOSAL: Derive theoretical bounds for the performance of branched dynamics algorithms with non-uniform terminal distributions, using techniques from optimal transport and concentration of measure, and exploring the trade-offs between the quality of the approximation, the computational cost, and the amount of prior knowledge about the system.
